interaction_type.value: shear-band-mediated plastic flow and particle stress shielding

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: In the FE simulation of the conventional Fe-TiB2 steel (homogeneous α-ferrite matrix), dislocation-mediated plasticity occurs predominantly through narrow shear bands oriented at ~45° to the loading axis; these patterns persist with increasing strain, leaving isolated nearly-undeformed zones (highlighted by red circles at ε = 11.0 %) caused by significant stress shielding from surrounding rigid particles, which compromises strength and ductility.

slip_behavior.value: Dislocation slip localises into narrow shear bands at ~45° to the loading axis within the homogeneous α-ferrite matrix (FE simulation, Fig. 12(a)); isolated stress-shielded zones remain nearly undeformed.

interface_notes.value: TiB2 particles in the reference steel are located at grain/phase boundaries and are micron-sized; the α-ferrite/TiB2 interfaces were represented in the FE model by zero-thickness COH3D8 cohesive elements with a bilinear traction-separation law (interface stiffness K = 10^6 MPa mm^-1; interface strength Tc = 700 MPa).

source.reason: The paper builds a second RVE with a single-phase α-ferrite matrix to simulate the conventional Fe-TiB steel, using the FEM setup (Fig. 2, periodic BCs) and the α-Fe parameters of Table 1.

simulation_method.value: Finite element method (FEM) using a 2D plane-strain representative volume element (RVE) constructed from an EBSD phase map (mapping algorithm for automatic meshing and phase assignment); element/mesh type CPE4 with a mesh size of 0.4 μm (500×500 elements). A second RVE with identical TiB2 distributions and boundary conditions but a single-phase α-ferrite matrix is used to simulate the conventional Fe-TiB steel.

boundary_and_initial_conditions.value: Periodic boundary conditions applied to the RVE edge node sets (edges a, b, c, d) per Eq. (1); reference point RP-2 fixed and RP-1 uniformly stretched along the x-axis direction (Fig. 2).

validation_against_experiment.value: The predicted tensile response for the conventional Fe-TiB2 steel (orange curve in Fig. 11(a)) is consistent with experimental results, demonstrating the reliability of the modelling approach.
